questions.q: What did Moses tell all Israel about his advancing age?
questions.a: He told them that he was now 120 years old and that he could no longer go everywhere that they could go.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Moses about going over the Jordan?
questions.a: He told Moses that he would not be going over Jordan but God would go over Jordan ahead of them and would destroy the nations there for Israel.

questions.q: Who did Yahweh say would go over Jordan instead of Moses?
questions.a: Yahweh told Moses that Joshua would go over the Jordan to lead Israel.

questions.q: What had Yahweh done to Sihon and to Og, the kings of the Amorites?
questions.a: Yahweh had destroyed them and their land.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say he will do for Israel when they meet the nations in battle?
questions.a: Yahweh says that he will enable Israel to conquer them when Israel meets them in battle.

questions.q: What instruction does Moses give to the Israelites?
questions.a: Moses tells them to be strong and courageous, not to fear, and not to be afraid of the nations because Yahweh will go with them and will not fail or forsake them.

questions.q: What did Moses say to Joshua while of all Israel was listening?
questions.a: Moses told Joshua to be strong and courageous for Joshua would go with the people of Israel into the land that Yahweh swore to their ancestors to give to them and Yahweh will cause them to inherit the land.

questions.q: What did Moses tell Joshua that Yahweh would do for him?
questions.a: Moses told Joshua that Yahweh would go before Joshua and be with him, and Yahweh would not fail or abandon Joshua so he should not be afraid or dismayed.

questions.q: To whom did Moses give the law after he wrote it?
questions.a: Moses gave this law to the priests, the sons of Levi, who carried the box and he also gave copies of it to all the elders of Israel.

questions.q: How often did Moses command the priests to read the law that Moses gave to them?
questions.a: Moses commanded the priests to read the law at the end of every seven years, during the Festival of Huts, in the hearing of all Israel.

questions.q: Why did Moses tell the priests to assemble the men, women, children, and foreigners?
questions.a: Moses told the priests to assemble all the people so that they could hear and learn, and honor Yahweh their God and keep all the words of the law and so that their children could hear and learn to honor Yahweh.

questions.q: For how long should the priests read the law to the people of Israel?
questions.a: The priests should read the law to the people for as long as they live in the land that they were going over the Jordan to occupy.

questions.q: What happen when Moses and Joshua presented themselves in the tent of meeting?
questions.a: When Moses and Joshua presented themselves in the tent of meeting, Yahweh appeared in the tent in a pillar of cloud which stood over the door of the tent.

questions.q: Why did Yahweh tell Moses to call Joshua and present themselves in the tent of meeting?
questions.a: Yahweh told Moses to call Joshua to the tent of meeting because the day was coming when Moses must die and Yahweh would appoint Joshua to be the new leader.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Moses he would do when the people break Yahweh’s covenant?
questions.a: Yahweh told Moses that on the day the people break his covenant, he would be very angry with them and would abandon them, and he would refuse to help them any longer.

questions.q: How did Yahweh tell Moses the people would act after Moses died?
questions.a: Yahweh told Moses that the people would become unfaithful to Yahweh and begin to worship the strange gods of the land and that they would forsake Yahweh and break the covenant that he had made with them.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Moses would happen to the people when Yahweh hid his face from them?
questions.a: Yahweh told Moses that many bad things would happen to them and he would stop protecting them.

questions.q: Why did Yahweh tell Moses to write a song and teach it to the people of Israel and make them memorize it?
questions.a: Yahweh told Moses to write a song and teach it to the people so that the song could be a witness for Yahweh against the people of Israel.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Moses the people would do when they were in the land that Yahweh swore to give to their ancestors?
questions.a: Yahweh told Moses the people of Israel would turn to other gods, worship them, despise Yahweh and break his covenant.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Moses the song would do when many evils and troubles happen to the people of Israel?
questions.a: Yahweh told Moses that the song would testify before Israel as a witness and it would not be forgotten by their descendants.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say he knew about the people even before he brought them into the land that he had sworn?
questions.a: Yahweh said that he knew the plans that the people were already making.

questions.q: How long did Moses wait before he wrote the song that Yahweh told him to write?
questions.a: Moses wrote the song on the same day that Yahweh told him to write it and then he taught it to the people of Israel on that same day.

questions.q: What command did Yahweh give to Joshua, the son of Nun?
questions.a: Yahweh commanded Joshua to be strong and courageous.

questions.q: Why did Yahweh command Joshua to be strong and courageous?
questions.a: Yahweh told Joshua to be strong and courageous because Joshua would bring the people of Israel into the land that Yahweh had sworn to them and Yahweh told Joshua that he would be with Joshua.

questions.q: To whom did Moses give the words of the law in a book when he had finished writing?
questions.a: Moses gave the words of the law to the Levites who carried the box of the covenant of Yahweh.

questions.q: What did Moses tell the Levites that they should do with the book of the law when he finished writing it?
questions.a: Moses told the Levites to take the book of the law and put is by the side of the box of the covenant of Yahweh their God so that it would be there as a witness against them.

questions.q: What did Moses tell the Levites he knew about them even while he was still alive?
questions.a: Moses told the Levites that he knew how they had been and would continue to be rebellious against Yahweh even after his death.

questions.q: Why did Moses tell the Levites to assemble before him all the elders of their tribes and their officers?
questions.a: Moses told the Levites to assemble the elders and officers so that he could teach them the song which would be a witness against them.

questions.q: What does Moses say that he knows will happen after his death?
questions.a: Moses says that after his death the people will utterly corrupt themselves and turn away from the path that Moses had commanded them.

questions.q: What does Moses say will happen when the people turn away from the path that Moses had commanded them?
questions.a: Moses says that disaster will come on the people in the following days after they turn away from the path that Moses had commanded them.

questions.q: Why does Moses say disaster will come to the people?
questions.a: Moses says disaster will come when Yahweh will become very angry because of the evil things they will do.

questions.q: What did Moses sing for all the assembly of Israel to hear?
questions.a: Moses sang all the words of the song he had written.

commentary.text: Moses encourages the people, and Joshua.
The law to be read every seventh year.
The Israelites' apostacy foretold, A song given to be witness against them.
The law delivered to the Levites.

Verses 1–8 Moses assures Israel of the constant presence of God with them. This is applied by the apostle to all God's spiritual Israel, to encourage their faith and hope; unto us is this gospel preached, as well as unto them; he will never fail thee, nor forsake thee, Heb 13:5. Moses commends Joshua to them for a leader; one whose wisdom, and courage, and affection they had long known; one whom God had appointed to be their leader; and therefore would own and bless. Joshua is well pleased to be admonished by Moses to be strong and of good courage. Those shall speed well, who have God with them; therefore they ought to be of good courage. Through God let us do valiantly, for through him we shall do victoriously; if we resist the devil, he will flee from us.

Though we read the word in private, we must not think it needless to hear it read in public. This solemn reading of the law must be done in the year of release. The year of release was typical of gospel grace, which is called the acceptable year of the Lord; for our pardon and liberty by Christ, engage us to keep his commandments. It must be read to all Israel, men, women, children, and to the strangers. It is the will of God that all people should acquaint themselves with his word. It is a rule to all, therefore should be read to all. Whoever has read of the pains taken by many persons to get scraps of the Scriptures, when a whole copy could not be obtained, or safely possessed, will see how thankful we should be for the thousands of copies amongst us. They will also understand the very different situation in which the Israelites were placed for many ages. But the heart of man is so careless, that all will be found too little, to keep up a knowledge of the truths, precepts, and worship of God.

Moses and Joshua attended the Divine Majesty at the door of the tabernacle. Moses is told again that he must shortly die; even those who are most ready and willing to die, need to be often reminded of its coming. The Lord tells Moses, that, after his death, the covenant he had taken so much pains to make between Israel and their God, would certainly be broken. Israel would forsake Him; then God would forsake Israel. Justly does he cast those off who so unjustly cast him off. Moses is directed to deliver them a song, which should remain a standing testimony for God, as faithful to them in giving them warning, and against them, as persons false to themselves in not taking the warning. The word of God is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of men's hearts, and meets them by reproofs and correction. Ministers who preach the word, know not the imaginations of men; but God, whose word it is, knows perfectly.

The solemn delivery of the book of the law to the Levites, to be deposited in, or rather by the side, of the ark, is again related. The song which follows in the next chapter is delivered to Moses, and by him to the people. He wrote it first, as the Holy Spirit taught him; and then spake it in the hearing of all the people. Moses tells them plainly, I know that after my death ye will utterly corrupt yourselves. Many a sad thought, no doubt, it occasioned to this good man; but his comfort was, that he had done his duty, and that God would be glorified in their dispersion, if not in their settlement, for the foundation of God stands sure.
